analysis: The changes are test-only. FlintAnswerStopTests.swift adds `case .logprobs: break` in FlintStreamOutcome.record (head line 130). FlintResponseFormatTests.swift changes `case .info: break` to `case .info, .logprobs: break` (line 362). Both make the switch statements exhaustive over MLXServerGenerationEvent after a new `.logprobs` case was added elsewhere. No production source, key handling, attestation, WebSocket, cache storage or authorization code is touched, so I found no regression against the TB-002, TB-007, TB-009 or TB-011 boundaries or against T-041 and the other listed threats. In these tests `.logprobs` is ignored, so they do not assert how logprobs interact with Flint answer-stop holdback or response_format validation. If the production change adds logprobs emission, a later pass should check whether logprobs for tokens belonging to a stripped stop sequence, or for content that response_format validation rejects, could leak text that the content stream withholds. That would be a consumer-facing leak of a held-back stop sequence or an invalid-output token. This test-only change cannot show that, and the production diff was not supplied here. I mark deeper review as needed only for that unseen production logprobs path. The test files give no evidence either way.
